schema_sql: CREATE TABLE jobs (row_id BIGINT NOT NULL, start_day BIGINT NOT NULL, end_day BIGINT NOT NULL, CHECK (start_day <= end_day))
original_sql: SELECT row_id FROM jobs WHERE start_day >= 10 AND end_day >= 10
reference_sql: SELECT row_id FROM jobs WHERE start_day >= 10
derivation: The ordering CHECK guarantees end_day >= start_day. Every legal row with start_day >= 10 therefore also has end_day >= 10, so the second conjunct is redundant.
source: data/SQL_Predicate_Family_Examples.sql, E2 seed from the team project proposal. This packaging is an offline scoring fixture, outside Martin's 32-task collection.
error_exposed: Keeping only end_day >= 10 incorrectly includes row 2 (start_day = 9, end_day = 10), which satisfies the ordering CHECK but fails the original start bound.
